import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Define the desired order for customer age groups for consistent plotting and legend
age_group_order = ['18-24', '25-34', '35-44', '45-54', '55+']

# Aggregate total sales by product and customer_age_group
# Use fill_value=0 to ensure all combinations exist, even if sales are zero
sales_by_product_age = df.groupby(['product', 'customer_age_group'])['total'].sum().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Ensure columns (age groups) are in the desired order for the stacked bars and legend
# Filter out any age groups that might not be present in the data, if any
existing_age_groups = [group for group in age_group_order if group in sales_by_product_age.columns]
sales_by_product_age = sales_by_product_age[existing_age_groups]

# Calculate total sales for each product to sort the products on the x-axis
product_total_sales = sales_by_product_age.sum(axis=1).sort_values(ascending=False)
sales_by_product_age = sales_by_product_age.loc[product_total_sales.index]

# Set a color palette for the age groups
colors = sns.color_palette("viridis", n_colors=len(existing_age_groups))

# Create the stacked bar chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 7))

sales_by_product_age.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=ax, color=colors)

# Add labels and title for clarity
ax.set_title('Total Sales by Product and Customer Age Group', fontsize=16)
ax.set_xlabel('Product', fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability if product names are long
ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45, ha='right') # 'ha' (horizontal alignment) makes rotated labels align nicely

# Customize legend
ax.legend(title='Customer Age Group', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
